newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end topsy-turvy day higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end topsy-turvy day higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures recovered toward midrange late, with most units ending higher after an afternoon of brisk, topsy-turvy trading.
Late in the day, day shorts who had taken advantage of the fast-paced midday slide decided to lock in profits and bail out, brokers said.
"Profittaking, I believe," said one trader after the close of reasons for the partial recovery in marks. "There were no huge players."
He also noted that June marks bounced back after basically respecting support at $0.5874, near the day's low.

Just before midday, marks abruptly skidded to a new session low, nearly erasing large early gains, as news emerged that the Bundesbank rejected a German government proposal to revalue the central bank's gold and currency reserves.
The Bonn government quickly retorted that it would stick with its plan anyway, essentially defying the central bank.
Brokers said the events created a rift between the two agencies that rattled confidence and undermined stability.
"I think the reaction really was that it amounted to political instability," added the broker. "People were buying (U.S.) dollars...there were no Swiss safe-haven plays at all."
Floor traders reported heavy buying from one firm, rumored on behalf of a large hedge fund, just before the quick knee-jerk drop sparked by the long-waited news.
Earlier, marks regained their footing after the Bundesbank denied a market rumor that Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer had resigned.
Futures had opened higher and barely jiggled when April U.S. durable goods orders rose 1.4 percent and gained 0.6 percent without defense. March's drops were revised upward.
Traders had expected respective gains of 1.3 percent and 0.8 percent last month in the typically volatile report.

The inability of the dollar to pierce 117.00 yen overnight, about $0.008571 in June futures, helped lift the yen, which also garnered support from a rally in Japanese stock and a rise in Japanese government bond yields overnight, brokers added.

June yen ended up $0.000070 at $0.008662, marks rose $0.0034 to $0.5900, Swiss francs added $0.0049 to $0.7097, sterling rose $0.0086 to $1.6388, Canadian dollar ended flat at $0.7238, Aussie dollar firmed $0.0003 to $0.7646, and Mexican peso lost $0.000050 to $0.125550.
